reader.decision: Go ahead: Aelita implements the three rulings in `mailer/config.py` and `mailer/bounces.py`, ready to deploy on 14 November. The cutover date stays at 14 November.
reader.decision_reason: The message records the 14 November cutover, which is 16 days before `smtp-old-1` goes offline on 30 November, so the month-end run goes through `smtp-mx-2`. The planned config and bounce changes match all three rulings. The retry arithmetic also holds: 3 retries at 1200 seconds fit in one hour, and 4 sends stay under the stated block threshold.

reconstruction.problem: `invoice-mailer` still sends through `smtp-old-1`, which goes offline on 30 November. The month-end invoice run starts that day. The open item was the cutover date to `smtp-mx-2`.
reconstruction.what_breaks: If the switch is not made before 30 November, every send fails and no customer gets a November invoice. That was shown in the earlier timeline. The message gives no other failure.
reconstruction.fix: Record Ruling 3 (cut over on 14 November). In `mailer/config.py`, set `SMTP_RELAY` to `smtp-mx-2.larkspur.internal`, `FROM_ADDRESS` to `invoices@mail.larkspur.io`, `BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT` to 3 (was 12) and `BOUNCE_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS` to 1200 (was 60). In `mailer/bounces.py`, make `handle_bounce` call `message.mark_failed()` at once on a hard bounce and never retry it. Deploy on 14 November.
reconstruction.cost: Not stated beyond the code edits. A recipient can bounce at most 4 times in one hour (the first send plus 3 retries), which the message says is under the `smtp-mx-2` block threshold of more than 5.
